payload.statement_nl:
Let [m]_q = (1-q^m)/(1-q), let (a;q)_k = ∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-a q^j), and let (a,b,c;q)_k = (a;q)_k (b;q)_k (c;q)_k. Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and let n > 1 satisfy n ≡ 1 mod 2d. Define
F_{d,r,n}(q) = ∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k,
and define
R_{d,r,n}(q) = [rn]_q q^{r(1-n)/2}.
Also define the modified summands by
H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - R_{d,r,n}(q),
and for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n-1,
H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k.
Then F_{d,r,n}(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = ∑_{k=0}^{n-1} H_{d,r,n,k}(q).

result_payload.proof_nl: Let T_k(q) = [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} / (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k. Then, by definition, F_{d,r,n}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} T_k(q). For k=0, each q-Pochhammer factor with subscript 0 is an empty product, hence equals 1. Therefore (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_0 = 1, (q^d;q^d)_0 = 1, and (q^{2d};q^{2d})_0 = 1; also q^{0(d-d*0-2r)/2} = 1 and [3d*0+r]_q = [r]_q. So T_0(q) = [r]_q. Consequently, F_{d,r,n}(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = T_0(q) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T_k(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = ([r]_q - R_{d,r,n}(q)) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} T_k(q). By the definitions of the modified summands, H_{d,r,n,0}(q) = [r]_q - R_{d,r,n}(q), and for every k with 1 <= k <= n-1 we have H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = T_k(q). Hence F_{d,r,n}(q) - R_{d,r,n}(q) = H_{d,r,n,0}(q) + sum_{k=1}^{n-1} H_{d,r,n,k}(q) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} H_{d,r,n,k}(q). This is exactly the stated identity.
result_payload.proof_summary: Split the defining sum for F into its k=0 term and the terms k>=1. The k=0 term equals [r]_q because every q-Pochhammer with subscript 0 is 1. After subtracting R, the resulting expression is exactly H_0 plus the unchanged summands H_k for 1<=k<=n-1.
